item.title: Program Associate
item.description: Join People Powered to help communities around the world have a greater say in the decisions that affect their lives! As Program Associate, you will support the design and delivery of People Powered's global capacity-building programs that help governments, civil society organizations, and community leaders adopt, strengthen, and scale participatory democracy. You will help implement training programs, accelerators, and learning cohorts that connect participants across countries and sectors, and create and curate content for People Powered's tools, online resource library, training courses, mentorship initiatives, and peer-learning activities. Salary: $60,000–$74,000 USD annually, adjusted for local cost of living. Deadline to apply: May 29, 2026.

item.title: Research Fellow and Strategy Fellow, Cause Prioritization Team
item.description: Coefficient Giving (formerly Open Philanthropy) is seeking Research Fellows and Strategy Fellows to join its Cause Prioritization team, focused on global health and wellbeing. Coefficient Giving is a philanthropic funder and advisor that has directed over $5 billion in grants since 2014 across areas including global health, scientific research, pandemic preparedness, potential risks from advanced AI, and farm animal welfare.
item.location: San Francisco, CA or Washington, DC

item.title: Development Associate
item.description: The Luminos Fund, an international nonprofit bringing education opportunities to the world's most vulnerable children, seeks a Development Associate to contribute to its rapid growth. The role includes providing systematic and administrative support for all fundraising and stewardship activities, including database and process management (Salesforce), gift processing and donor recognition, and prospect research. The position reports to the Director of Development and is based full-time in Boston, Massachusetts. Salary range: $50,000–$65,000 USD.

item.title: Job Developer
item.description: Youth Justice Network (formerly Friends of Island Academy), founded in 1990 to support young people released from Rikers Island, seeks a full-time Job Developer for its Career Services Center in the Bronx, NY. The Job Developer will create and maintain a network of employer relationships to support career development and job attainment for justice-involved young adults ages 18–40. Responsibilities include employer outreach, strategic candidate placement, résumé coaching, interview preparation, and post-placement follow-up. Bachelor's degree and minimum two years of workforce development experience required. Bilingual Spanish preferred. Salary: $60,000–$65,000. Apply with résumé and cover letter to careers@youthjustice.org.

item.title: Operations Coordinator/Associate
item.description: Coefficient Giving is seeking an Operations Coordinator/Associate to support its Business Operations team in San Francisco or Washington, D.C. Responsibilities include supporting staff with administrative tasks (travel booking, purchasing, mail), managing and improving SF and DC office spaces, providing executive assistance to directors and senior staff, coordinating org-wide events including quarterly Togetherness Weeks, and assisting the IT team with onboarding and tech support. Coordinator roles are open to candidates without specific experience; Associate roles require at least four years of relevant experience. In-person from SF or DC office required; relocation support available.
item.location: San Francisco, CA or Washington, DC

item.title: Government Relations Intern (Students)
item.description: Appian is looking for a Government Relations Intern to operate at the intersection of public policy and business value. You will support Value Engineering efforts, helping quantify and communicate the economic and operational impact of Appian's technology to government stakeholders. Responsibilities include policy analysis of legislative developments and agency initiatives (DoD, DHS, VA, HHS); building ROI models and business cases; drafting briefing materials and talking points for Congress and senior agency officials; monitoring the competitive landscape; and supporting Capitol Hill and agency engagement meetings. This internship is based at Appian's headquarters in McLean, Virginia, with periodic travel to Washington, DC and Capitol Hill. In-office 5 days a week. Summer 2026. Undergraduate students only.

item.title: Government Affairs Intern
item.description: The State of South Carolina is seeking a Government Affairs Intern to support government affairs and legislative engagement activities. This is an internship opportunity with a South Carolina state agency, providing hands-on experience in public administration, government relations, and state policy. Candidates should be currently enrolled in an accredited college or university with a major related to public administration, public policy, political science, communications, or a related field.

item.title: Health Policy Analyst
item.description: LMI, a digital solutions provider dedicated to accelerating government impact, is seeking a Health Policy Analyst to support work for the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), specifically the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS). The successful candidate will join a team delivering policy, operations, and analytical support. The primary focus is facilitating compliance and monitoring efforts to ensure program participants are aligned with federal regulations, sub-regulatory guidance, and all programmatic requirements. This position does not involve direct drafting of policy or influencing policy decisions. This position may be performed remotely. LMI is headquartered in Tysons, Virginia.

item.title: Innovation Policy Research Intern
item.description: SRI International's Center for Innovation Strategy and Policy (CISP) in Arlington, Virginia is seeking an Innovation Policy Research Intern to contribute to innovation policy research, analysis, and evaluations for a diverse range of clients. Work spans technology-based economic and workforce development, innovation ecosystem assessment, innovation strategy and training, complex program evaluation, federal science and technology program support, and advanced analytics in R&D analysis. Responsibilities include collecting, managing, and analyzing diverse data sets; applying proprietary and other analytical approaches; supporting quality control; producing high-quality reports and presentations; and providing administrative support. U.S. Citizenship required. Must be pursuing a four-year degree in a STEM field, public policy, or policy-oriented social or hard sciences.

item.title: Associate Program Specialist
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 6/27/2026.
ICF is a global advisory and technology services company with approximately 9,000 employees, working across public and private sector clients in areas including health, energy, social programs, defense, and international development. The Associate Program Specialist will support the launch and implementation of key programs, working alongside senior program managers and client-facing teams to ensure efficient operations and delivery across functional areas.
Key responsibilities include: providing administrative and operational support for program activities; coordinating with field-based staff and external stakeholders including trade allies, utility clients, and community partners; monitoring and maintaining program records, databases, and tracking tools; preparing program status reports, memos, and documentation; assisting with quality control for deliverables; and participating in team meetings and client briefings to relay program progress.
Qualifications: A bachelor's degree in a relevant field such as public policy, business, environmental studies, or communications is required. Prior internship or entry-level experience in program administration, consulting, or a government/nonprofit environment is preferred. Strong organizational and communication skills, proficiency in Microsoft Office (especially Excel and Outlook), and the ability to manage multiple priorities are essential. ICF offers a competitive benefits package including tuition reimbursement, 401(k) matching, and flexible workplace arrangements.
For full position details and to apply, please visit the original posting.

item.title: Governmental Affairs Associate
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 6/27/2026.
The Association County Commissioners of Georgia (ACCG) is a nonprofit instrumentality of Georgia's county governments, serving as the consensus-building, training, and legislative organization for all 159 county governments in the state since 1914. The Governmental Affairs Associate coordinates policy development processes, researches and shapes state and federal policy, and advocates on behalf of ACCG membership. The position reports to the Director of Governmental Affairs.
Key responsibilities: Assist with coordinating policy development for key functional areas of county government; promote the Association's legislative initiatives and positions and represent the association before the Georgia General Assembly, Congress, and state and federal agencies; monitor, review, analyze, summarize, and report on legislation at the state and federal level to determine impact on counties; receive and respond to inquiries from counties, legislators, state agencies, media, and the public; prepare written material for the Association's magazine, newsletters, social media, and handbooks; work with ACCG Policy Committee Chairpersons to develop meeting agendas; serve on federal, state, and regional advisory committees; and facilitate district visits and meetings. Position requires travel within Georgia with occasional overnight travel.
Qualifications: Bachelor's degree with coursework in political science, criminal justice, law, planning, public administration, or a related field, plus 1–3 years of experience in public policy with extensive writing, communication, and public speaking experience. Must have thorough knowledge of county government in Georgia and demonstrated ability to build relationships with elected officials, media, and diverse stakeholders.
Salary starts from $70,000 annually. ACCG is an equal opportunity employer.

The State of Minnesota is seeking qualified professionals to join its workforce in policy-related roles that support the delivery of essential government services to Minnesota residents. Minnesota state government employs professionals across a wide range of policy, program, and administrative functions, offering competitive benefits and meaningful public service careers.
Key responsibilities for state policy and program roles typically include: analyzing state and federal legislation and regulations for impact on agency programs; preparing policy briefs, reports, and recommendations for agency leadership; coordinating with stakeholder groups, advocacy organizations, and legislative staff; implementing program changes in response to policy updates; and tracking program performance metrics and compliance requirements. Minnesota values public servants who are committed to equitable service delivery and continuous improvement.
Qualifications: A bachelor's degree in public policy, public administration, political science, or a related field is typically required. Relevant experience in state or local government, nonprofit, or policy research settings is preferred. Strong analytical writing, communication, and organizational skills are essential. Minnesota state employees receive comprehensive benefits including health insurance, retirement plan, and generous leave policies.
For full position details, requirements, and to apply, please visit the original posting at USAJOBS.

item.title: Foreign Assistance Program Analyst
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 6/27/2026.
Guidehouse is a global AI-led professional services firm delivering advisory, technology, and managed services to the commercial and government sectors, with approximately 18,000 professionals across energy, financial services, healthcare, national security, and defense. The Foreign Assistance Program Analyst will join a Washington, DC-based team supporting U.S. government clients — likely the Department of State or USAID — in the oversight, analysis, and implementation of foreign assistance programs.
Key responsibilities include: conducting program and policy analysis of foreign assistance portfolios; monitoring program performance, budgets, and compliance with federal regulations; preparing briefing materials, reports, and presentations for senior government and Guidehouse stakeholders; coordinating with interagency partners, implementing organizations, and field-based personnel; supporting data collection and management activities; and contributing to strategic planning and program improvement efforts across global development and security assistance accounts.
Qualifications: A bachelor's degree in international affairs, political science, public policy, economics, or a related field is required; a master's degree is preferred. Relevant experience in foreign assistance, international development, government contracting, or consulting is strongly preferred. Strong written and oral communication skills, ability to analyze complex programs and policy environments, and proficiency in Microsoft Office are essential. A security clearance may be required or preferred. Guidehouse offers competitive salaries ($98,000–$163,000 range for senior roles, entry/mid-level compensation varies), comprehensive benefits, and a discretionary bonus.
For full position details and to apply, please visit the original posting.

item.company: Institute for the Study of War (ISW)
item.title: Researcher
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 6/27/2026.
The Institute for the Study of War (ISW) is a non-partisan, non-profit public policy research organization dedicated to advancing an informed understanding of military affairs through reliable research, trusted analysis, and innovative education. ISW is committed to improving the nation's ability to execute military operations and respond to emerging threats to achieve U.S. strategic objectives. ISW researchers produce timely open-source intelligence analysis for policymakers, warfighters, and the general public on conflicts including Russia-Ukraine, the Middle East, and China-related security issues.
The Researcher will conduct open-source research and analysis of geo-strategic dynamics affecting U.S. national security interests. Responsibilities include: conducting detailed open-source intelligence analysis of current conflicts and security threats; writing and publishing analytical reports and short-form intelligence products; editing and overseeing daily written products to meet institutional writing standards; collaborating with the research team to generate intelligence products; and supporting the planning, preparation, and execution of public events and private briefings. ISW researchers work directly with senior analysts and contribute to shaping policy recommendations.
Qualifications: A bachelor's degree in a field related to ISW's core mission (international relations, political science, area studies, national security) is required; a master's degree is preferred. Demonstrated analytical writing ability and expertise in a relevant geographic or functional area (e.g., Russia, Middle East, China, defense policy) is required. Critical language skills (Russian, Arabic, Mandarin, Hebrew, Ukrainian, Persian, etc.) are a plus. ISW provides formal professional development in war studies, analytic methods, and policy writing. This is a full-time, in-person role in Washington, DC.

item.company: NORC at the University of Chicago
item.title: Research Associate I – Health Care Programs Research
item.description:
NORC at the University of Chicago is an objective, non-partisan research institution that delivers reliable data and rigorous analysis to guide critical programmatic, business, and policy decisions. Since 1941, NORC has conducted groundbreaking studies and advanced principles of scientific integrity across health, social science, and public policy domains. The Research Associate I will join the Health Care Programs Research Department, a team providing data-driven research, policy and program analysis, and technical assistance to federal and state government agencies and foundations on Medicaid, Medicare, Marketplace coverage, and broader health system transformation.
Key responsibilities include: providing general research support on health policy research and technical assistance projects; conducting literature reviews, environmental scans, and statistical analysis of primary and secondary data; preparing memos, tables, graphs, and report outlines; taking meeting notes and drafting minutes; supporting business development through background research on programs, award history, and client objectives; and developing project materials such as visual exhibits and serving as an editor for deliverables.
Qualifications: A bachelor's degree in social science, public health, health policy, or a related field is required. At least 6 months of research experience (internships included) in health research, public health, or health policy using qualitative and/or quantitative methods is required. Some understanding of Medicaid, Medicare, and other public insurance programs is expected. Knowledge of statistical software (SAS, SPSS, NVivo, Tableau) is preferred. Strong written and verbal communication, attention to detail, and collaborative teamwork skills are essential.
Salary: $56,000 annually. Comprehensive benefits include subsidized health insurance (effective day one), dental, vision, defined contribution retirement, paid parental leave, and tuition assistance. This is a hybrid role with a minimum of six days per month in the Washington, DC office. Application deadline: June 7, 2026. A resume and cover letter are required; a writing sample may be requested.

item.title: Researcher / Sr. Researcher, Energy Systems & International Development
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 6/27/2026.
Mathematica applies expertise at the intersection of data, methods, policy, and practice to improve well-being around the world, collaborating closely with public- and private-sector partners to translate big questions into deep insights. The company is 100% employee-owned and conducts work in health, education, early childhood, nutrition, employment, disability, and international development. This Researcher or Senior Researcher position will support anticipated evaluations in the energy sector in low- or middle-income countries (LMICs), designing and executing user-focused evaluations that help donors, practitioners, and policymakers improve programs and make data-driven decisions.
Key responsibilities include: serving as technical expert on evaluations of diverse energy sector investments (grid expansion, off-grid systems, utility performance, renewable energy, energy efficiency, and energy systems planning); advising on data sources and coordinating with technical stakeholders to obtain administrative and grid-level data; integrating open-source and widely available energy/climate data platforms into MEL work; conducting key informant interviews with program participants, engineers, utility staff, policymakers, and donors; providing written summaries and analyses of findings; and performing landscape assessments, case studies, and political economy analyses of the energy sector in LMICs.
Qualifications: A postgraduate or doctoral degree in electrical engineering, physics, environmental/climate science, energy economics, energy policy, or related field is required. Minimum five years of experience working in the energy sector in a low- or middle-income country, including deep understanding of policy/regulatory frameworks, generation, transmission, distribution technologies, and energy finance is required. Familiarity with evaluation methodologies and quantitative/qualitative research methods is needed. Fluency in English; proficiency in French strongly preferred. Willingness to travel to project locations required. Note: If an offer is extended, it is contingent upon successful award of relevant work.
Salary: $120,000–$135,000 (Researcher) or $140,000–$155,000 (Senior Researcher), plus annual bonus and comprehensive ESOP/benefits package.

item.title: Energy & Sustainability Researcher for Energy Efficiency Programs (Arlington, VA – 2026 Grad)
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 6/27/2026.
ICF is a global advisory and technology services company with approximately 9,000 employees working at the intersection of business analysis, policy, digital strategy, and data science. ICF's energy practice helps utilities, government agencies, and private-sector clients design and evaluate energy efficiency programs, delivering rigorous research and analysis that drives sustainability goals and program improvement. This role is specifically designed for 2026 graduates entering the energy research field.
As an Energy and Sustainability Researcher for Energy Efficiency Programs, you will support the design, implementation, evaluation, and reporting of energy efficiency programs for utility and government clients. Key responsibilities include: conducting market research, literature reviews, and data analysis on energy-related topics; supporting program evaluations through data collection, statistical analysis, and report drafting; preparing written reports and presentations of findings for clients; assisting with survey design and data management activities; and collaborating with a multidisciplinary team of energy professionals, economists, and data scientists.
Qualifications: A bachelor's or master's degree in environmental science, energy policy, economics, public policy, engineering, or a related field (2026 graduate) is required. Strong analytical, quantitative, and written communication skills are essential. Familiarity with statistical software (R, Python, Stata, Excel) is preferred. An interest in energy efficiency, demand-side management, or sustainability programs is important. ICF offers a comprehensive benefits package including tuition reimbursement, flexible workplace arrangements, 401(k) with match, and paid community involvement opportunities.
For full position details and to apply, please visit the original posting.

item.title: Sr. Global Trade Analyst
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 6/27/2026.
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars — including Falcon, Starship, Dragon, and Starlink programs. The Sr. Global Trade Analyst will support SpaceX's global trade compliance team on these programs, based in SpaceX's Washington, DC office.
As a Sr. Global Trade Analyst, you will support SpaceX's global trade compliance team on Falcon, Starship, Dragon, and Starlink programs, with a focus on export control matters. You will work closely with attorneys, other legal and compliance professionals, and engineers to ensure that SpaceX complies with applicable U.S. export control laws and is able to conduct launches and other operations in a timely fashion. Key responsibilities include: conducting research on U.S. federal statutes, regulations, directives, and guidance related to export laws (EAR, ITAR, OFAC); reviewing technical documentation and advising on export classification and licensing requirements; supporting internal compliance investigations; managing export and import licensing applications and correspondence with government agencies; and helping define and implement global standards for trade compliance data within item master records.
Qualifications: A bachelor's degree is required; a degree in international affairs, legal studies, engineering, or a related discipline is preferred. 4–6 years of relevant experience in global trade compliance, export control, or national security law is required, with demonstrated focus on customs and import compliance. Strong knowledge of ITAR, EAR, and related U.S. export regulations is essential. SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Note: an active security clearance may be required for certain mission-critical work.
For full position details and to apply, please visit the original posting.

item.title: Government Programs Specialist
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 6/27/2026.
Applied Intuition is powering the future of physical AI. Founded in 2017 and valued at $15 billion, the company creates the digital infrastructure needed to bring intelligence to every moving machine on the planet — serving automotive, defense, trucking, construction, mining, and agriculture industries through tools and infrastructure, operating systems, and autonomy solutions. Eighteen of the top 20 global automakers, as well as the United States military and its allies, trust the company's solutions. Applied Intuition is headquartered in Sunnyvale, CA, with offices in Washington, DC, and globally.
The Government Programs Specialist will operate at the intersection of Applied Intuition's defense and government technology portfolio and its federal customer base. Key responsibilities include: supporting business development and capture activities for defense and federal agency programs; coordinating proposal development, contract management, and program execution activities; tracking program milestones, deliverables, and compliance requirements; engaging with government stakeholders and program offices to understand requirements and communicate solution value; conducting policy and regulatory research related to defense technology, acquisition, and autonomy; and supporting internal strategy development for the defense and government sector.
Qualifications: A bachelor's degree in public policy, political science, national security, international affairs, business, or a related field is required. Prior experience in government contracting, defense acquisition, federal program management, or policy analysis is strongly preferred. Strong organizational, communication, and analytical skills are essential. Familiarity with the federal acquisition process (FAR/DFARS), DoD programs, or AI/autonomy technology is a plus. Applied Intuition is an in-office company; employees are expected to work from the Washington, DC office five days a week.
For full position details and to apply, please visit the original posting.

item.title: NATO International Staff Position
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 6/27/2026.
NATO, the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, is an intergovernmental military alliance of 32 member nations committed to collective defense and security. NATO's international headquarters in Brussels employs civilian staff across a wide range of policy, analysis, communications, administrative, and operational functions in support of the Alliance's political and military decision-making structures.
NATO International Staff positions support the organization's core missions, which include collective defense, crisis management, and cooperative security. Staff members may work within political affairs, communications, finance, human resources, information technology, legal, or strategic policy functions. Responsibilities vary by position but generally include: conducting policy research and analysis; preparing briefings, reports, and position papers for NATO leadership; coordinating with national delegations and partner organizations; supporting NATO's strategic communications and public diplomacy efforts; and contributing to the planning and execution of NATO ministerial meetings and summits.
Qualifications: Candidates for NATO civilian positions typically need a university degree in international relations, political science, law, security studies, or a related field. Prior experience in international organizations, government, think tanks, or policy research is valued. Excellent English communication skills are required; French is an asset. NATO staff are recruited on the basis of merit from member nations, and positions are open to nationals of NATO member countries. Salary and grading are set according to NATO civilian pay scales.
For full position details and to apply, please visit the original posting at nato.taleo.net.
